sentences.text: 1  NC: 2025:KHC-K:6649  MFA No. 202425 of 2023 HC-KAR  THIS MFA IS FILED UNDER SECTION 173(1) OF MOTOR VEHICLES ACT, PRAYING TO MODIFY THE JUDGMENT AND AWARD JUDGMENT AND AWARD DATED 02.11.2022 PASSED BY THE SENIOR CIVIL JUDGE AND MACT, BASAVAKALAYAN, IN M.V.C.NO. 579/2017, BY ENHANCING THE COMPENSATION.

THIS APPEAL COMING ON FOR ADMISSION, THIS DAY,
JUDGMENT WAS DELIVERED THEREIN AS UNDER:
CORAM: HON'BLE MRS JUSTICE P SREE SUDHA  ORAL JUDGMENT 1.

This appeal is preferred by the claimant against the Judgment and award dated 02.11.2022 passed in MVC No.579/2017 by the Senior Civil Judge and MACT, Basavakalyan (for short 'the tribunal')
seeking enhancement of the compensation.
2. The injured claimant aged 20 years working as operator in Waghmore milk Diary and earning a sum of Rs.10,000/-, met with accident on 17.02.2017 and suffered grievous injuries.
He took treatment in the Hospital.
He filed claim petition before the tribunal seeking compensation of Rs.15,00,000/- along with interest.

After NC: 2025:KHC-K:6649 HC-KAR considering the entire evidence on record, the tribunal awarded a sum of Rs.4,71,190/- along with interest at the rate of 6%
per annum from the date of petition till the date of realization.
Being aggrieved by the said Judgment and award the claimant preferred the present appeal seeking enhancement of the compensation awarded by the tribunal.
3. In the present appeal it is contended that, the claimant examined P.W.2 the Doctor.
The Doctor issued disability certificate which is marked at Ex.P.11.
As per the disability certificate, the doctor assessed the disability of the claimant at 38%, but the tribunal has taken only 10%.
The claimant was admitted in the Hospital on 17.02.2017 and discharged on 24.03.2017.
He was hospitalized for 37 days.
The claimant sustained multiple grievous injuries.
The amounts granted under different heads by the tribunal are on lower side and no amount is granted under the head loss of amenities.

Thus,
he requests for enhancement of the compensation.

sentences.text: 2 4. Heard the arguments of the learned counsels from both sides.

5. Though he was working as operator in Waghmore Milk Dairy and earning a sum of Rs.10,000/-,
he has not filed any income proof to prove his income.
In view of the guidelines issued by the Karnataka State Legal Services Authority, the income of the claimant for the year 2017 is to be taken at Rs.10,250/-.
The tribunal has rightly taken the income of the claimant at Rs.10,250/- which needs no interference.
The claimant examined the Doctor.
As per the wound certificate the claimant sustained III Comp. fracture, left medial mallous with dislocation of left patella and CLW on left popliteral foss, which are grievous in nature.
The Doctor assessed the disability at 38% to the whole body, but the tribunal has taken 10% instead of 13%.

Therefore, the loss of future income comes to :
Rs.10,250/- X 12 X 18 X 13% = Rs.2,87,820/-
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6649 HC-KAR 6.

The Tribunal has granted Rs.2,09,790/- towards medical expenses and it needs no interference.
7.
The appellant was admitted in the hospital for 37 days.

Considering the nature of injuries and period of hospitalisation, this Court finds it reasonable to grant an amount of Rs.75,000/- for pain and suffering, Rs.25,000/- for loss of amenities and Rs.30,000/- for transportation, extra nourishment and attendant charges.
8. The appellant might not have attended any work at least for a period of three months due to the injuries sustained.
Therefore, he is entitled for an amount of Rs.30,750/- (Rs.10,250 x 3) for loss of income during laid up period.
9. The Tribunal has also granted Rs.10,000/- towards future medical expenses and it needs no interference.

10. Hence, the appellant is entitled for the modified compensation under different heads as below:
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6649 HC-KAR Pain and suffering Rs.75,000/-
Medical expenses Rs.2,09,790/-
Future medical expenses Rs.10,000/-
Loss of future earnings Rs.2,87,820/-
Loss of income during laid up period Rs.30,750/-
Transportation, extra nourishment, Rs.30,000/-
and attendant charges Loss of amenities Rs.25,000/-

Total Rs.6,68,360/-
Less: awarded by Tribunal Rs.4,71,190/-
Enhancement Rs.1,97,170/-

11. In the result, the following order is passed:
( i) Appeal is allowed in part.
(ii) The appellant/claimant is entitled for the enhanced compensation of Rs.1,97,170/- with interest at 6% per annum from the date of petition till the date of realisation.
NC: 2025:KHC-K:6649 HC-KAR (iii) Respondent No.2-Insurance Company is directed to deposit the aforesaid compensation amount within one month from the date of this judgment.
(iv) On such deposit, the appellant is permitted to withdraw the entire amount along with interest accrued on it.
